topics.topic: How operation_element_conclusion is derived across statuses, executions, attempts, and approvals
questions: What conclusion does this operation return for an operation element whose NodeExecution is `refused_by_owner`, `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`, since those statuses are not all failures under A13's closed failed-status rule and are not among the listed result variants?
When an operation element has several NodeExecutions because of `not_sent` retries or a resend after `not_applied`, which execution and EffectAttempt determine `effects.operation_element_conclusion`?
May this operation also read EffectApproval records, and what precedence determines the conclusion when an element has several historical executions, attempts and approvals?

quotes: operation_element_conclusion: [BEHAVIOR] MUST trust the run, pinned version and element its caller passes and check none of them; it reads the element's NodeExecutions through read_records with ExecutionsOfElement, its EffectAttempts with AttemptsOfElement and its approvals with ApprovalsOfElement, and the binding's output ports through read_flow_version of the run's flow_version_id and read_binding of the node's binding_id; the trace is its only source.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.
judgement.why: The later notes specify the records read, select the highest-attempt execution, and define status and approval precedence.

topics.topic: Required input and expected-output port sets for authored trial cases
questions: Must an authored trial case contain exactly the contract's input ports, and what happens to an extra input name that is not a contract port?
When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it specify only a subset; and is an empty object equivalent to absence?

Must trial inputs contain exactly all and only the contract input ports, and, when expected outputs are present, must they contain exactly all and only the output ports, or may expected outputs be partial?
Must inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extra names, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output rather than a partial expectation?

judgement.divergence: One implementer rejects an authored trial case containing an input or expected-output name that is not a contract port, while another ignores the extra name and accepts the case; the authoring caller notices refusal versus acceptance and the resulting corpus differs.
judgement.why: The later notes require every declared input port, and every output port when expected outputs are present, but never say how extra port names are handled.

topics.topic: Unit used for masked failure-detail length
questions: In what unit is the masked failure detail's length measured?
Is the disclosed length the stored UTF-8 byte length, Unicode scalar count, or another measure?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the unit of masked failure-detail length.

precedent.topic: Unit used to measure disclosed masked failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later notes explicitly define the disclosed length as the UTF-8 byte length.

topics.topic: Scope of manifest checks performed by check_installed_instances at startup
questions: Which A08 rule 5 checks are 'checks of the record itself' during `bindings.check_installed_instances`, and are they applied to every capability, only capabilities relevant to credentials, or only the service and selected-instance structure?
Which A08 rule 5 checks apply at startup when this operation has no operation name or proposed ports with which to perform the operation-specific checks?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the scope and ordering of startup manifest validation.

precedent.topic: Startup manifest validation scope, checks, and ordering for credential-bearing services
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes restrict startup validation to operation-independent service-record checks and credential-header collisions for selected instances.

topics.topic: Agent masking representation for personal-data many-file ports
questions: What does an agent receive for a personal_data value on a many file port, where the durable representation is an ordered list of SpooledFiles and no aggregate file-list digest is defined?

topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and exact path composition
questions: Which additional URL components are allowed in `api_base_url`—userinfo, query, fragment, or an existing path—and exactly how are trailing slashes and the declared path combined without client normalization changing the request?

topics.topic: Body processing for successful bindings without output ports
questions: For a 2xx response to a binding without output ports, is the body still read to the ceiling, checked for a credential echo, and failed when oversized, or is it truly ignored?

topics.topic: Cleanup policy for unreferenced content-addressed bytes
questions: May unreferenced file bytes remain permanently in the content-addressed area after a failed change, or must they be removed so trial-case fixtures remain the only persistent files?

topics.topic: Complete spool_file error mapping
questions: Does `spool_file` return `internal_error` for an occupied recorded position, symbolic link or I/O failure, in addition to the listed ceiling refusal?

topics.topic: Deadline testing and remaining-time interface
questions: What callable operation or value is the promised way to test the deadline, and may callers also obtain remaining time for blocking I/O?

topics.topic: Depth and scope of store ownership and permission checks
questions: Must `store.open_store` verify ownership and permissions recursively for every existing database, content file, fixture, spool directory, and spool file, or only for the data directory itself?

topics.topic: Deterministic tie-breaking for equivalent flow edges and constants
questions: What breaks ties between two edges with the same endpoints but different guards, or two constants targeting the same port, so identity computation and the first proof failure are deterministic when those items occur in either input order?

topics.topic: Exact requirements of the sandbox startup probe
questions: What exact code, inputs, bounds, mounts and assertions constitute the probe, and which sandbox facilities must it exercise before startup succeeds?

topics.topic: Fields included in a run answer
questions: Does the run answer also expose the Run model's inputs, pinned_implementations, resumptions and cancelled_by, or is the quoted list exhaustive?

topics.topic: Handling corrupt or incompatible existing stores
questions: What must `store.open_store` do when an existing database or store layout is corrupt, unreadable, incomplete, or from an incompatible kernel schema version?

topics.topic: Handling successful trial outputs above the stored-value size limit
questions: What does `functions.try_implementation` or admission record when a successful sandbox execution returns a value output above `stored_value_bytes_max` but within the contract's `output_bytes` bound?

topics.topic: How callers inspect historical FlowActivations referenced as authority
questions: How can a caller inspect the historical FlowActivation named as a draft-write EffectAttempt's authority after another activation has replaced it?

topics.topic: How content_identity selects the applicable identity and sorting recipe
questions: How does the operation know which record identity recipe and list-sorting rules apply, particularly when it receives an arbitrary value such as an idempotency-key object, request description or manifest capability entry?

topics.topic: How immutable files are accessed at a pinned manifest revision
questions: How is a file read 'at' `manifest_revision`, and what guarantees that repeated reads during one process observe that immutable revision rather than mutable files at `manifest_location`?

topics.topic: Input representation accepted by canonical_bytes
questions: Does `canonical_bytes` receive raw JSON text so it can detect duplicate object keys, or an already parsed JSON value in which duplicate keys have been lost?

topics.topic: Propagation of record_change ordinal refusals
questions: When this store refusal reaches functions or runs, which do not define a conversion for it, is it exposed to the MCP caller as refused, converted to internal_error and followed by process shutdown, or declared unreachable?

topics.topic: Recovery behavior for already resolved effect attempts
questions: During recovery, which resolved attempts are reached again? In particular, must an attempt resolved `applied` be treated as concluded without calling `reach_operation_element`, while only `not_applied` is reached to request fresh approval?

topics.topic: Referential integrity checks and error classification in record_change
questions: What exact links and referential constraints must each named change validate, and which violations are refused versus internal_error?

topics.topic: Validation and failure ordering for binding port schemas
questions: Must `bindings.propose_binding` and `bindings.accept_binding` reject input or output port schemas outside the supported JSON Schema subset, and where does that check occur in A08 rule 5's failure order?

topics.topic: Validation timing and error classification for flow and constant schemas
questions: When are unsupported or invalid schemas on flow inputs, flow outputs, and constants rejected, and is the result a composition refusal, a proof failure, or an invalid request?

topics.topic: Whether get_repair_view returns read_slot history or only the repair snapshot
questions: Is the whole-history result of functions.read_slot returned to the caller, or is it used only internally while the repair view returns the current contract, current implementation, current corpus and recent executions required by K-12?

topics.topic: Whether open_store returns a handle or establishes global store state
questions: Is the returned open store a handle that every later store call must receive, or does `store` retain one process-global opened instance internally and return only confirmation?

topics.topic: Whether sandboxed agent code may access the exchange directory
questions: May agent-written code open, create, and read files inside the exchange directory, or is that directory accessible only to the runner for transferring declared inputs and outputs?

topics.topic: Whether seeded deterministic pseudorandom APIs are permitted
questions: Does the prohibition on randomness include deterministic pseudorandom APIs with an explicit seed, or are those APIs intentionally permitted?
